🌍 Macro Context — Oct 11, 2026

Buffett Indicator 234% 🔴 ALL-TIME EXTREME
S&P Forward P/E ~19x (vs. ~17-19x long-run avg)
Trend → Flat-to-down off the 237% May 2026 record

Market cap is still 2.3x US GDP — near its all-time record, a level every prior reading above ~190% has preceded a drawdown. But the forward P/E tells a calmer story: 19x is only slightly rich versus the ~17-19x long-run average, because 2026 earnings grew ~39% YoY and caught up to price — not classic bubble math, more "priced for continued delivery."

Implication: this isn't a reason to force new entries, but it's also not a flashing stop-everything signal the way a cheap-earnings/high-multiple combo would be. Keep stops tight regardless — a valuation unwind from a Buffett Indicator this high would be fast.

Last historical episodes near this level: 2000 dot-com peak, 2021 COVID-bubble peak.

🔔 SPXC — almost certainly already closed, 48 calendar days unreconciled

Two independent live-IBKR snapshots (via stock-finder, Sept 29 and Oct 6 — 8 days apart) both show only GOOG open and cash at $432.16, not the $330.60 this file still carries. The cash delta ($101.56) matches the 0.5-share $205 GTC exit-limit filling (gross $102.50, net ≈$101.50) far better than the $186.90 stop — this was a small-profit limit exit, not a stop-out. portfolio.json has not been synced in 48 days despite this being flagged repeatedly.

Action: confirm the fill in IBKR (price/date) and run portfolio-manager to remove the SPXC line and reset cash_available to ~$432.16. This is now purely mechanical — the data has agreed with itself for 12 days running.

⚠️ GOOG — stop status unconfirmed, 32 days blind

Stop is a plain STOP at $333.90 (Abbas's explicit choice, OCA-bracketed with TP1 $408). No live quote for 32 straight days. Best unverified read from search: third-party quote pages this week cluster around $340-344, which would be ~2-3% clear of the stop and consistent with every snapshot since mid-September — a multi-week pattern, not a one-off, so the balance of evidence says the stop hasn't fired. Still not a confirmed quote. Needs a direct IBKR check before you'd want to rely on this for a decision.

💵 Cash deployment

portfolio.json shows $330.60 cash; the best available evidence (two independent IBKR snapshots) says it's actually ~$432.16 once SPXC's exit is recognized. Deploying against either number right now means sizing a new position off data you already know is wrong on one side. Hold off on new entries until the SPXC/cash sync above is done — then re-run this check (or stock-finder for a fresh candidate) against the correct figure. No fresh discovery candidate generated here by design.

📚 Today you learned

Flash / Preliminary Revenue Releases

US companies report earnings once a quarter, all at once. Several large Asian issuers — TSMC chief among them — also publish unaudited monthly revenue, usually within the first 10 days of the following month, because Taiwan's exchange rules require it. That's why TSM's Q3 top line was already public on Oct 8 (record NT$1.49T, +50% YoY, beating both analyst consensus and the top of management's own $44.6-45.8B guidance) a full week before the Oct 15 earnings call. The flash number kills the "revenue surprise" — what's left to move the stock on the 15th is margin and forward guidance, not the top line. If you ever trade a Taiwanese ADR (TSM, UMC) around earnings, check for the monthly flash print first; the "beat" you're trading may already be priced in days before the formal release.

Also today: Margin guidance bands — TSM guides gross margin as a 2-point range (65-67% this quarter), not a point estimate, because foundry costs (yield, node mix, utility/power) swing quarter to quarter in ways revenue mix doesn't fully predict.
